correctness.rationale: For each ordered colour pair, a depth-one formula names exactly its realized column type. If the ordered support is asymmetric, a depth-two horizontal diamond of a missing reverse type names a whole row; otherwise equality of ordered types is a back-and-forth bisimulation across rows. These statements prove exactly |E| or 2|E| atoms and the depth cutoff. Support constructions give the sharp maximum and nonmonotonicity. Surjective occupancy counts via t! Stirling(m,t), transpose-invariant supports via (1+z)^q(1+z²)^{q(q−1)/2}, and a union-bound/single-defect expansion prove the random law. Direct finite refinement checked 17,208 coloured models; all 511 and 65,535 nonempty supports were additionally enumerated for q=3,4. No infinite conclusion rests solely on finite tests.

value.rationale: The object is a naturally parameterized generated bimodal Boolean algebra on a rectangular product Kripke frame, and atom count is precisely the number of modally distinguishable states. The result supplies a complete structural classification, a tight uniform maximum despite unbounded column count, a sharp depth cutoff, a provable decrease under adding worlds, and an exact probability law under a canonical independent valuation model. None is a routine numerical increment or a disconnected finite census; it clarifies which structural symmetries erase modal distinctions.
